title: What If You Miss Your Old Sexual Lifestyle?
paragraphs:
What If You Miss Your Old Sexual Lifestyle?
The Secret Grief Nobody Talks About After Choosing Jesus
There are nights you don’t talk about.

Nights where your room is quiet, but your mind isn’t. Nights where your body remembers what your spirit has already renounced. Nights where you stare at the ceiling and wonder if something is wrong with you… because a part of you still misses what God told you to leave behind.
And you hate that you miss it.
No one warned you about this part.
They told you about freedom. They told you about deliverance. They told you about being made new.
But they didn’t tell you that sometimes, freedom still aches.
They didn’t tell you that leaving your old sexual life behind can feel like grieving a relationship that once felt alive… even if it was destroying you.
So here you are.
Saved… but still remembering.
Free… but still tempted.
Changed… but not numb.
And the enemy whispers, “If you miss it, maybe you never really changed.”
But that’s not the voice of God.
Because Scripture never promised you wouldn’t feel the pull.
It promised you power over it.
In Galatians 5:17, Paul writes something brutally honest:
In the original Greek, “σὰρξ” (sarx) means the flesh, the human nature inclined toward sin. And “ἐπιθυμεῖ” (epithumei) means to crave, to long for, to desire intensely.
That means the struggle you feel isn’t proof of failure.
It’s evidence of war.
And war only exists where two sides are alive.
Before Christ, there was no war. You didn’t fight it—you followed it. You didn’t resist—you indulged it. You didn’t question—you justified.
But now?
Now something inside you resists what you used to run toward.
That’s not weakness.
That’s transformation beginning to breathe.
But let’s be honest.
There were moments in that old life that felt good.
Moments of closeness.
Moments where you felt wanted.
Moments where loneliness disappeared, even if only temporarily.
And your flesh doesn’t remember the consequences first.
It remembers the pleasure.
James 1:14-15 says:
“Each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire…”
The Greek word for “lured” is “ἐξελκόμενος” (exelkomenos), like a fish being drawn out by bait.
Temptation doesn’t show you the hook.
It shows you what glitters.
It shows you the memory without the regret.
The feeling without the emptiness.
The connection without the confusion.
And for a moment… you almost forget why you left.
But you did leave.
Not because it never felt good.
But because it was never truly good for you.
There’s a difference.
Hebrews 11:25 speaks of “the fleeting pleasures of sin.”
Fleeting.
Temporary.
Passing.
In Hebrew thought, the idea of temporary pleasure is often tied to what fades like vapor—here for a moment, gone the next, leaving you emptier than before.
And if you’re honest…
It did leave you empty.
After the texts stopped.
After the bodies separated.
After the moment passed.
You were still searching.
Still restless.
Still wanting something deeper.
Because what your soul was craving was never just physical.
It was spiritual.
Connection.
Covenant.
To be fully known without shame.
And that kind of intimacy doesn’t come from lust.
It comes from God.
In Genesis 2:24, the Hebrew word for “one flesh” is “בָּשָׂר אֶחָד” (basar echad).
Not just physical union.
Total unity.
Body, soul, and spirit aligned under God’s design.
What you were tasting before wasn’t that.
It was a counterfeit.
A shadow of something sacred, stripped of its covering.
So yes…
You might miss it.
But what you miss isn’t always what you think.
You don’t just miss the act.
You miss the feeling of being wanted.
You miss the illusion of closeness.
You miss the temporary silence of your loneliness.
But Jesus doesn’t offer illusions.
He offers truth.
And truth sometimes hurts before it heals.
In John 8:36, Jesus says:
“So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.”
The Greek word for “free indeed” is “ὄντως ἐλεύθεροι” (ontos eleutheroi).
Truly free.
Genuinely free.
Not just behavior modification… but heart transformation.
And real freedom doesn’t mean you never feel tempted.
It means you’re no longer controlled.
So when you miss your old sexual lifestyle…
Don’t panic.
Don’t spiral.
Don’t assume you’ve gone backward.
Instead, recognize what’s happening.
Your flesh is remembering.
But your spirit is choosing.
And every time you choose Christ over craving…
Something eternal is being built inside you.
Even if it doesn’t feel like it.
Especially when it doesn’t feel like it.
This is where most people quit.
Not because they don’t love God…
But because they’re tired of fighting feelings they thought would disappear.
But following Jesus was never about feelings disappearing.
It was about truth becoming stronger than feelings.
And sometimes that truth whispers, not shouts.
“Stay.”
“Hold on.”
“Don’t go back.”
Because what’s ahead of you is holier than what’s behind you.
You’re not losing something.
You’re being prepared for something sacred.
A love that doesn’t leave you confused.
A connection that doesn’t make you question your worth.
A future where intimacy is covered by covenant, not chaos.
But you have to walk through this tension to get there.
So if you’re in that place right now…
Missing it.
Fighting it.
Trying not to go back…
Be honest.
Not as a performance.
But as a confession.
Because you’re not the only one.
And your honesty might give someone else the courage to stay too.
And if you’re serious about walking deeper with Jesus—not just in moments like this, but daily—stay close.
Follow.
Because you weren’t meant to fight this alone.
And if God is using this to speak to you… support what is feeding your spirit.
Not out of pressure.
But out of purpose.
You’re fueling discipleship.
You’re helping truth reach people who are drowning silently.
More than that…
If you want to go deeper, stay rooted, and grow in Christ, this is where it begins:
Because this isn’t just about resisting sin.
It’s about becoming someone new.
And that process?
It’s messy.
It’s painful.
It’s holy.
So don’t run from the tension.
Let it transform you.
Because one day, you won’t just look back and say, “I survived that.”
You’ll say, “God used that to change me.”
And that old life you miss?
It won’t even recognize who you’ve become.
You don’t actually miss your past… you’re just learning how to live without chains.
